To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
APL is the process of gaining academic credit for learning from work or life experience, and that APEL is the process of claiming academic credit based on prior experience and learning.
APL and APL are two distinct but related processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of a credit system that values and recognises the knowledge and skills that people have acquired through their experience.
developing a model of accreditation for learning gained through experience and the use of this model in the development of APL and APL systems.
the ways in which learning gained through experience is recognised and valued by higher education institutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the process of learning is an important part of a person’s life.
the process of learning is a continuous process and that learning can take place at anytime and at any place.

the APL/APELS process is about valising and empowering practitioners, it is a way of turning experience into academic learning, it is a reflection of a person’s learning and it is a way to award credit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to show the value of the APL/APEl process in terms of the benefits to the individual, the employer and the institution.
the APEL process is one which values and empowers practitioners.
we have shown how APL/APELP could be used in the context of an online learning environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the APL and APLE processes can be used to turn experience into academic credit.
the APL and APL process is a valuable tool for the development of practitioners.
there is a strong case for the introduction of APL and APLEL in all higher education institutions, and that this is a process which is not difficult to achieve.
